newsitem.title: PERU: Hostages, relatives have exchanged 812 messages.
newsitem.headline: Hostages, relatives have exchanged 812 messages.

text.p: Hostages held in Peru have exchanged a total of 812 written messages with their relatives but future mail deliveries will be limited to one every three days, the Red Cross said on Thursday.
The hostages in the Japanese embassy residence in Lima have been allowed by their Marxist captors to send and receive notes on special forms brought in and out by Red Cross go-betweens.

Red Cross spokesman Roland Bigler told a news conference the hostages had sent 272 messages to their relatives since the residence was stormed on Dec. 17, while family members had written 550 notes to the captives.
"We are going to establish this exchange of messages every three days since we have to check the content here and the police and the MRTA command have to check the content," Bigler said.
Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels seized the residence during a cocktail reception to press demands for the freeing of jailed comrades.

The notes and handwritten signs held up periodically to a window, are the only forms of communication the hostages have with the outside world. Phone links to the residence were cut by authorities in the early stages of the crisis.
There was no sign of an early end to the siege on Thursday.
